This was my second visit to Angelina’s Kitchen, and it’s so good that I gladly make the trip all the way from the Bronx. The restaurant is beautiful, spacious, and conveniently located in an area with plenty of shopping, making it a great destination for lunch or dinner.

The service is truly impeccable. Every member of the staff is attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about the menu. They made us feel well taken care of from the moment we walked in, and even prepared a special off-menu dish for us, which made the experience feel even more personal.

The food is incredibly fresh, and you can really taste the quality of the ingredients. One of my favorite parts of the meal is always the focaccia—it’s warm, flavorful, and the perfect way to start your dining experience.

My only small criticism is that, as someone who doesn’t eat seafood, I wish there were a few more à la carte options. That said, if you’re a seafood lover, this place is an absolute gem. The menu offers an impressive selection, and it’s easy to see why so many people love it.

I’ll definitely be back again. The exceptional service, fresh food, and overall experience make the drive completely worth it.

Angelina’s Restaurant in Staten Island was the perfect place to celebrate our 6-month anniversary, and the experience truly went above and beyond anything we expected. From the moment we arrived, the atmosphere felt special, romantic, and unforgettable. The decor is absolutely beautiful, blending Valentine’s Day romance and elegant wedding-style charm with a warm Christmas spirit. The candle-lit, dim lighting creates a high-class, intimate allure that immediately sets the tone for love and celebration.

What made the night even more meaningful was the hospitality. I highly recommend Angelina’s for couples going on dates, celebrating anniversaries, Valentine’s Day, wedding engagements, or any special romantic occasion. This was an unforgettable experience, and we will definitely be returning.

Went here for Mother’s Day and unfortunately had one of the most frustrating dining experiences I’ve had in a long time, especially for an $86 per person prix fixe menu.

The menu included an appetizer, first course, second course, main, dessert, and coffee/tea, with several options for each. On paper, it sounded great. In reality, the execution was awful.

To start, I’m gluten free, which was communicated from the beginning, my husband even called ahead to confirm accommodations. Our server seemed completely unfamiliar with gluten allergies/intolerance. One server actually tried to tell me a breaded croquette was gluten free and only because I questioned it myself and asked what the crust was made of, another told our server  it was breadcrumbs and then asked, “is that okay?” Absolutely unacceptable.

The appetizer was probably the best part of the meal — a mozzarella ball and a few slices of salami — but even that felt like the restaurant was trying harder to look fancy than actually serve quality food. Everything after that was incredibly underwhelming.

Then came the wait. TWO HOURS passed before we even saw our second course. ( only having apps for two hours is inconceivable in my mind ) Our server disappeared almost entirely, and our table was getting visibly upset trying to figure out where our food even was. When the pasta dishes finally arrived, mine was missing. After more waiting, my gluten free pasta came out almost crunchy, clearly rushed because they forgot it. Then our main courses arrived immediately after the pasta, making it obvious the timing of the meal was completely mishandled.

My steak was also cooked nowhere near what I ordered. I asked for rare to medium rare, leaning more rare, and received something closer to medium well.

Service overall was extremely poor. Our server lacked warmth from the very beginning, took our orders, disappeared for most of the night, and offered little to no communication throughout the delays. Desserts and coffee also took longer.
At one point the host offered to remove our drinks (two bottles of Stella) but didn’t look reflected on the bill

The only positives were the bartender, who was kind and helpful when taking dessert orders, and the host, who at least tried to be sociable and accommodating.
For the price point, the experience was disorganized, poorly managed, and honestly exhausting. Definitely not the special Mother’s Day dinner we expected.

What truly made the evening special was the incredible service. Our server Thomas was attentive, knowledgeable, friendly, and made sure every detail of our meal was perfect. It's rare to find service that genuinely elevates the entire dining experience, but Thomas did exactly that!!

We were also grateful when Chef Philly came out to greet us and even assist Thomas with brining out  some of our food. Phil takes such pride in his work and he is the reason we came to the restaurant.

My husband and I have been under a lot of stress lately, and this dinner was exactly what we needed. For a few hours, we were able to relax, enjoy amazing food, and feel truly cared for. On top of everything else, we found the pricing to be very reasonable for a steakhouse of this quality.

Thank you to Thomas, Chef Philly, and the entire team at Ruddy & Dean for an unforgettable night. We will absolutely be back and highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for outstanding food, exceptional service, and a first-class dining experience.

Thanks!
John & Danielle

This is not the usual practice in Boston.

text.text: Ok, let me start my honest review by commending the efforts of what appeared to be a day that was short on staff, on Father’s Day at that. It was not too crowded or busy and there were 2 maybe 3 waitresses covering tables, bar and the front. In fact when we walked in we waited 10 minutes before someone greeted us and seated us. Totally fine we get it wasn’t a big deal at all, but it was the little details through out the evening that add to overall experience. We received menus, drink menus and was told there is an extensive beer menu on a board in front of the restaurant to which I couldn’t see from my table, I just told the waitress to pick any one from the category I liked. It’s cool, but details.  We ordered our food a kids meal, 2 ribeyes and a chicken parm.    My wife asked for chicken parm with additional sauce on the side they brought her chicken parm with zero sauce on it just a small bowl of sauce on the side, she also added it was flavorless. Our steaks came out cooked perfectly to our preference but incredibly bland. It would have been nice to have a steak sauce available (at least a house made) or anything other than the additions you can add to your steak for a fee, to which we ordered but added nothing to flavor or enhance a bland tough steak (it was the onions sauce and the bordelaise sauce). And yes I say “tough steak” although it was cooked perfectly medium, I have no answer to that. Again small details, minor disappointments that add to an overall experience. The sides were bland, mash potatoes were stiff and bland, creamy spinach was not soft taste quickly prepared. Overall not what I expected from a highly rated steakhouse. The service and atmosphere was that of a restaurant just opening and working out the kinks. Like I said the Staff was kind and as attentive as can be but the food was just not good.  This could very well be an off night. And honesty I thought about not writing a review but maybe they’ll read this and hopefully hear the genuine constructive intent and make some adjustments…. Or not.  I wish them well and hope they continue to grow.

Cole’s Dockside has definitely become a new favorite. I highly recommend it if you’re looking for delicious food and a genuinely great time. Can’t wait to come back!

text.text:

Of particular note was the ambiance.   It's a small space but after looking carefully, you can see that the decorations did not interfere with their floor space.  It definitely aids with the experience.

text.text:
When I first saw the exterior of this restaurant, I was absolutely intrigued. The ornate carvings, majestic statues, and shimmering golden doors beckoned me to come in. The place was crowded and everyone seemed to be enjoying their meal.

Upon being seated in one of the elaborate chairs, I had to pause and take in the visual feast around me. The cozy interior was adorned with 360 degree of stunning ornate collectibles from Sri Lanka, exquisite tchotchkes adorning the walls and hanging from the ceilings, creating a continuous visual stimulus.

The hostess greeted me and explained that I could either scan the menu code or enjoy the wonderful lunch buffet for $21. (Since I visited during the weekend lunch hour, I'm unsure if the price changes at other times.) Noticing that everyone else was enjoying the buffet, I decided to follow suit, and I'm so glad I did.

I'm a huge fan of Sri Lankan cuisine, and the buffet was a delight. They have hot entrées in shallow cauldrons that are constantly being refilled. The spread consisted of many vegetarian delights alongside a few meat entrées, such as deviled chicken and pork curry. My personal favorites were the eggplant, dal lentils, and the kale and coconut salad. Their papadam was light and delicious, so definitely don't skip those! Along another wall, the dessert station featured sago, chocolate, caramel, mango, and gooseberry puddings. The latter two were my absolute favorites.
